questions.q: Where do you start analyzing a log?
options: With GPS quality and satellite count over the whole flight
questions.explain: A cut-off log means power loss; high vibration makes everything else worthless.

questions.q: The VIBE threshold above which altitude/position problems are almost certain?
questions.explain: Below 30 is normal, above 60 means problems almost for sure.

options: Loss of the radio link to the transmitter
questions.explain: 2 — radio, 11 — GPS, 16 — EKF variance, 17 — EKF failsafe, 29 — vibration compensation.

questions.q: Which ATT fields do you compare to spot a mechanical problem?
questions.explain: A sharp divergence between desired and actual means a failure or lack of thrust.

options: Telemetry as the GCS saw it
An ESC firmware log with telemetry
questions.explain: The telemetry the GCS saw over the radio link: lower rate and with gaps, but it survives even if the SD card burned up.

questions.q: What do you use to read a .bin in Python?
CTUN.ThO = 0.78 with sagging voltage in Loiter indicates:
questions.explain: Throttle at the ceiling with sagging voltage; BAT.Volt/Curr confirm it.

questions.q: What do you enable in LOG_BITMASK for PID tuning?
options: Only GPS and IMU at full rate
questions.explain: PID (PIDR/PIDP/PIDY) and batch sampling while tuning; turn them off afterward, the log grows.
